description: Tests and largely retracts qou-bq9l's use of the fractional-twist mechanism. TWO CORRECTIONS. First, the cumulative achievable set is dense: the union of t over n <= 24 covers 43 of the 45 rationals with denominator <= 12 (96%, only 4/9 and 7/8 missing), so a 'substrate only produces rational ratios' prediction has no discriminating power, and all eight exact group-theoretic targets tested (QCD 3bar/6 = 2, QCD singlet/octet = 8, piN 9 and 9/2, quark-model 3/2 and 5/3, 4, SU(6) 25/9) trivially hit it. Second and decisive, cumulative is the wrong object: a physical system has a FIXED strand count — two quarks n=2, a nucleon n=3, two nucleons n=6, 4He n=12 — and per n the admissible sets are small (n=9: 3 values; n=12: 3; n=15: 6; n=18: 7). At n=2, n=3 and n=6 there is NO admissible fractional twist at all: t in (0,1) needs c(lambda) strictly between -n/2 and 0, and at n=6 the achievable content sums are {-15,-9,-5,-3,0,3,5,9,15} while the window needs {-1,-2}; at n=2 the only candidate gives t = 1 exactly, the excluded boundary. CONSEQUENCES: the two-nucleon sector, which is n=6 and is where qou-v3u2 proved the impossibility lives, cannot be repaired by this mechanism; and the t = 1/3 QCD hit is realised at n=12 while two quarks are n=2, so it is withdrawn as evidence. What stands from qou-bq9l is the mechanism itself — c_n^n = Delta^2, block magnitude exactly q^(2c(lambda)/n), fractional values from n=5, and a sparse closed-form per-n availability table.
caveats: THIS PROBE RETRACTS PART OF qou-bq9l, WHICH IS MINE. Its mechanism (c_n^n = Delta^2, magnitude q^(2c/n), fractionality from n=5) is re-verified and stands. Its cumulative enumeration as a predictive claim, and its t = 1/3 coincidence as evidence, do not. Anyone quoting that probe should quote this one alongside it.

THE PER-n ANALYSIS ASSUMES A SYSTEM'S TWIST MUST COME FROM ITS OWN STRAND COUNT. That is the natural reading — the Coxeter element of B_n is defined on n strands — but a construction could in principle embed a subsystem in a larger braid and inherit a twist from there. Nothing here rules that out; it would need the embedding exhibited, and the resulting object would no longer be the n-strand system's own Coxeter element.

The eight group-theoretic ratios are used ONLY to demonstrate that the cumulative test has no power. They are not claimed as predictions, matches, or targets the substrate should meet, and no per-n check against them is offered — at the strand counts where they would be posed (n=2, n=3) there is nothing to check against.
